scope: P4-TSUNAMI-20 semantics; no runtime or public-contract change

tsunami.meaning: tsunami phenomenon in official warning/information or observation context

tsunami_potential.meaning: explicit source-reported potential for an event to generate a tsunami

rules: Expected wave height is not observed wave height.
Expected arrival is not observed arrival.
Missing numeric source value is not zero wave height.
Textual source states such as Currently Observing or Currently Investigating must not be converted into invented numeric values.
Generic severity must not be converted into wave height.

bmkg.current_weather_router_path: source-reported tsunami potential on latest earthquake

invariants: Tsunami potential is not an official tsunami warning.
Earthquake is not automatically tsunami.
Tsunami potential is not an observed tsunami.
Tsunami hazard type alone does not prove an observed wave.
Warning stage is not wave height.
Expected wave height is not observed wave height.
Expected arrival is not observed arrival.
JMA tsunami observation is not a warning event.
Cancellation does not prove that no tsunami occurred.
No Threat from one center is not a global no-tsunami statement.
Information is not an active warning stage.
GDACS is not a primary tsunami warning authority.
NOAA responsibility areas are not global tsunami warning coverage.
JMA Japan coverage is not automatically NWPTAC international coverage.
BoM Australia coverage is not automatically IOTWMS TSP global coverage.
Missing geometry is not outside_coverage.
Endpoint reachability is not coverage proof.
Provider ID is not a scoring axis.
Profiles remain deny-only.
Cross-provider deduplication is not introduced.
decisions_for_p4_tsunami_30: Design additive event semantics for tsunami alert stage and active-threat state without replacing existing hazard_type.
Preserve provider-specific alert labels while exposing a normalized canonical stage.
Represent expected and observed wave timing/height in distinct fields.
Correct JMA observation semantics to observation_kind=observation.
Correct BMKG potential semantics to seismic_network/seismic_event_catalog/observation while retaining source_class=event_indicator and hazard_type=tsunami_potential.
Define point/bbox eligibility when JMA and BoM events lack embedded geometry.
Keep domestic warning roles distinct from NWPTAC/IOTWMS international advisory roles.
Keep GDACS separate as disaster awareness.
Do not add provider priority or cross-provider deduplication.

authoritative_references.finding: NTWC and PTWC have designated service areas; PTWC also has international forecast-center roles.
JMA issues tsunami warnings/advisories for coastal forecast regions based on tsunami generation estimates.

authoritative_references.source: JMA Tsunami Warnings/Advisories and Tsunami Information
authoritative_references.finding: JMA distinguishes warning/advisory, forecast information and observed tsunami arrival/height information.

authoritative_references.source: JMA Northwest Pacific Tsunami Advisory Center
authoritative_references.finding: NWPTAC is a distinct international advisory role supporting recipient-country warning decisions.

authoritative_references.source: Australian Bureau of Meteorology - About Tsunami Warnings
authoritative_references.finding: JATWC distinguishes watch, no-threat bulletin and warning; warning may follow observation confirmation or imminent impact.
JATWC warns Australia and separately acts as an Indian Ocean Tsunami Service Provider.
InaTEWS publishes tsunami early-warning bulletins, observation updates and warning terminations; this is separate from the current WeatherRouter open earthquake potential indicator.
